def get_settings() -> Settings:
    """Return the process-wide Settings singleton, built on first access.
    Instantiating ``Settings`` at import time made ``import backend.config``
    fail (env/secrets validation) before callers could configure anything, so
    the singleton is created lazily on first ``settings`` attribute access.
    """
    existing = globals().get("settings")
    if existing is not None:
        return existing
    instance = _finalize_settings(Settings())
    globals()["settings"] = instance
    return instance

def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any:
    if name == "settings":
        return get_settings()
    raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")

coverage_gaps: NEW DEFECT, not in any packet record — HIGH VALUE, code defect (resolver-owned), NOT a contradiction. backend/domains/payments/models/payment_models.py:147-158 — PaymentIntent.__table_args__ places the dict {"schema": "payments"} as the FIRST tuple element instead of the LAST. SQLAlchemy requires the schema dict last; placing it first raises at class-definition time: `sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: 'SchemaItem' object, such as a 'Column' or a 'Constraint' expected, got {'schema': 'payments'}` raised from backend/domains/payments/models/payment_models.py:134 (class PaymentIntent). Verified: `python -c 'import domains.payments.models'` -> FAIL ArgumentError; `import domains.payments.models.payment_models` -> FAIL ArgumentError. The three sibling classes in the SAME file place the dict correctly and last (payment_models.py:46, :81, :111), which is why only PaymentIntent breaks. Why it has not crashed the app: main.py never imports this module (verified — 'domains.payments.models.payment_models' in sys.modules == False after `import main`, and Base.metadata contains zero payments.* tables), so the defect is latent but the whole payments model layer is dead code. Fix is mechanical: move {"schema": "payments"} to the last element of the tuple. This is the closest thing to record 1 and 2's 'payments' subject matter and should be routed to a dimension covering model/schema declarations.

SECOND, RELATED NEW DEFECT (same module, different mechanism) — LOW/MEDIUM. Backend/modules/employee/routers/hr.py (55921 bytes, 97 routes) is unreachable dead code shadowed by the hr/ package. Confirmed three ways: (a) importlib.util.find_spec('modules.employee.routers.hr').origin == backend/modules/employee/routers/hr/__init__.py with submodule_search_locations not None (IS PACKAGE: True); (b) backend/modules/employee/routers/__init__.py:17 imports 'hr', which resolves to the package; (c) route-set diff gives 97 routes in hr.py vs 97 in the package, differing only in POST /employees/{employee_id}/kill-switch (dead) vs POST /admin/{code}/employees/{employee_id}/kill-switch (hr/employees.py:107, live). The only functional consequence found is that the kill-switch path differs between the two, and the LIVE one is the package's — so no user-facing route is currently lost. Law 8 (one router file per domain) and Law 135 (all router files listed in routers/__init__.py) are both satisfied only by accident. This is already recorded as 07_CONTRADICTIONS.md CONTRAD-034, so it is not a new finding — flagged here because SIX records in this packet (11-16) cite the dead file as their backend authority and I had to re-verify all six against the live package.
